correctness.rationale: For arbitrary \(0<t\le 1/2\), the primary source's exact postselection inequality gives the penalty \((1+t)t^{-1}\log_2 g_{n,d}\); its uniform expansion near \(\alpha=1\) gives \(Q^\downarrow_{1+t}\le Q^{(1)}+a t+c t^2\). Combining these with coherent-information monotonicity yields the finite-block bound. The code-fidelity inequality follows by substituting the same bound into source Eq. (31) and rearranging. The choices \(t=\sqrt{L/n}\) and \(t=\Delta/(2K)\) are admissible under the stated hypotheses, and the inequalities leading to the \(6K\) denominator are elementary and replayed by the included verifier. No finite experiment is used as proof of the channel inequalities.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source fixes \(\alpha=1+n^{-1/2}\), obtaining \(O(\log n/\sqrt n)\) and a fixed-gap strong converse. Its inspected full text does not state the free-parameter optimization, the \(O(\sqrt{\log n/n})\) coherent-information bound, or the shrinking-gap fidelity bound. Searches for aliases involving symmetric-input quantum capacity, postselection, coherent information, moderate deviations, and optimized Rényi order found no covering statement. Generic de Finetti and classical-communication moderate-deviation results address different objects and do not imply this theorem.
residual_risks: A very recent or differently indexed manuscript could independently optimize the same Renyi parameter and not yet appear in the inspected indexes.
A general one-shot theorem under different terminology might imply an equivalent shrinking-gap bound after specialization, although targeted searches did not identify one.
No optimality of the resulting window is claimed, so stronger second-order or moderate-deviation converses may exist for special channel classes.

value.rationale: The improvement is not a cosmetic constant change: it lowers the universal symmetric-input coherent-information correction by a factor \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and upgrades the source's fixed-rate strong converse to rates whose excess above \(Q^{(1)}\) vanishes. This directly sharpens the source's finite-block benchmark for searches over symmetric codes and identifies a nontrivial moderate-deviation exclusion window. The result uses the exact polynomial postselection dimension and channel-uniform second-order Rényi control; it is not a finite enumeration or a renamed special case.
